'''Claude Bouchiat''' ({{IPA|fr|klod buʃja}}; 16 May 1932 – 25 November 2021) was a French physicist, and a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Claude Bouchiat |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-B/claude-bouchiat.html |website=l'Académie des sciences |access-date=28 January 2024}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Graduate of the [[École Polytechnique]] in 1955. He completed a Ph.D. in 1960 titled ''La règle de sélection ΔT=0 dans les transitions de Fermi et la théorie de l'interaction vectorielle en radioactivité β''.<ref>{{cite thesis | last=Bouchiat | first=Claude | title=La règle de sélection ΔT=0 dans les transitions de Fermi et la théorie de l'interaction vectorielle en radioactivité β | year=1960 | oclc=43453614 | language=fr | page=}}</ref>

Bouchiat was director of research at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] in the theoretical physics laboratory of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] from 1971 to 2003. Claude was the disciple of [[Louis Michel (physicist)|Louis Michel]] and worked with him on the [[anomalous magnetic dipole moment]] of the [[muon]].

Bouchiat became an honorary research director in 2003.

{{ill|Philippe Meyer (physicist|lt=Philippe Meyer|fr|Philippe Meyer (physicien)}} and Bouchiat supervised the doctorates of [[Joël Scherk]] and [[André Neveu]] at [[University of Paris XI]] in [[Orsay]].

===Personal life===
Bouchiat married [[Marie-Anne Bouchiat]] who is also a physicist. Their daughter [[Hélène Bouchiat]] and son [[Vincent Bouchiat]] are both [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicists]].<ref name=x1953>{{cite web |url=https://1953.polytechnique.org/Itineraires/Bouchiat.html |title=Claude Bouchiat |last= |first= |date= |website=1953.polytechnique.org |publisher= |access-date=2023-12-11 |quote=}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Bouchiat |first=Vincent |date=1997 |title=Quantum fluctuations of the charge in single electron and single Cooper pair devices |publisher=[[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]]  |oclc=1040947759 |url=https://theses.fr/1997PA066241 |quote=Enfin, j'ai une pensée toute particulière pour mes parents, Geneviève, Hélène, et Behnaz pour leur soutien constant durant toutes ces années.}}</ref>

Bouchiat died on 22 November 2021, at the age of 89.<ref name="bio"/>

== Distinctions ==
* 1980: Elected correspondent of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in the Physics section<ref>[http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-B/claude-bouchiat.html List of members of the French Academy of Sciences]</ref>
* 1983: [[Prix Ampère]] de l’Électricité de France by the French Academy of sciences
* 1990: [[Three Physicists Prize]] by the École normale supérieure de Paris<ref>[http://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/BouchiatC_bio1008.pdf Notice biographique de Claude Bouchiat, Correspondant de l’Académie des sciences, PDF]</ref>
